A statement about the rule and the session, never a permission and not a refusal; every family recheck still applies.

challenges.description: One entry per proof family, fixed order CAPITAL_COMMAND then ACCESS_ADMIN. Each says which precondition POST /step-up enforces for that family (request body field `family`) and whether it holds for the caller now. Either ACTIVE-able proof satisfies the same step-up-requiring rows. Not a promise the password will be accepted.

session_step_up.description: This session's own step-up fact, the one the capital mutations recheck (a capital-family or an access-admin-family proof, whichever is live), plus, per proof family, whether the step-up route precondition holds for the caller. A capital delegate needs no access.grant/revoke: the CAPITAL_COMMAND precondition is a current own ALLOW of a step-up-requiring action. Not a promise the password will be accepted; no new authentication mechanism and no capability.

AccessEligibilityBatch.description: FE-068. Up to eight resources x the same 1-16 actions in one current-only self read. Each resource carries exactly the rows of portal.self-eligibility.v1 (same evaluator, same reasons, same target rules) plus a typed step_up_state. Resources are unique (runtime-enforced) and every result carries the same actions in the same order (runtime-enforced: JSON Schema cannot compare sibling arrays). An action unsupported by one resource is a typed per-resource refusal, not a batch failure. Advisory only: no permit, no lease, no target existence, no source/field qualification; per-family checks and the real step-up recheck remain authoritative.

default_workspace.description: The workspace the server resolves for this member, or a typed absence. Never a choice between several: more than one candidate is AMBIGUOUS (sorted by workspace_id, at most 16; more is UNAVAILABLE, never a first-N). A candidate is a workspace the caller is a CURRENT MEMBER of. OWN_CURRENT_GRANT_RECORD says a stored, unrevoked, in-interval ALLOW record of the caller exists under that workspace's current reviewed policy revision: a hint for choosing a workspace, NOT proof of an effective right (navigation/eligibility for the chosen workspace evaluate the full graph). No peer, role or other-member fact is ever published.

self_entry.description: A self-only presentation for the member's OWN access review, distinct from the owner/admin policy matrix (/administration/profile-access, whose guards are unchanged). It is backed by the existing own effective read only and needs no peer-user selector or administration fetch. AWAITING_CONSUMER_ROUTER: the client must implement this route before navigating to it.

account_operations.description: The account-management mutation is NOT commissioned: the credential rotation behind the "Rotate credential" control is the PM REVISE_BINDING (credential-only) family, for which Portal has no route (binding.change.propose proposes only) and no qualified source. A typed refusal that holds for every member, never a permission; step_up_required is null (not determined, never false). The identifiers are display names, NOT capability names, and a navigation or menu fact never opens this mutation. A temporary client token such as execution.accounts.manage has no server authority and must not gate it.

AccessSelfContext.description: FE-057/058/038. The member's own session context, current-only and advisory: the default workspace (or a typed absence), the self-only entry route and the typed no-operation branch for account management. Takes no query. Cross-field producer invariants (valid_until_ms > observed_at_ms, candidates unique and sorted, one access_basis per ambiguity, self-entry route never under the admin matrix route) are runtime-enforced and stated here. Not a permit, not source readiness; every read and command rechecks current authority.
